label: Catholic natural law as formalized here is satisfiable
meaning: Catholic natural law as a complete theory in the metaethics question set (#185): goodness is actuality (ST I q.5 a.1), evil is privation of a due good (q.48 a.3), moral judgments have truth (I-II q.94 a.4), the Germans' error (a.4), and the first precept (a.2) are jointly satisfiable. Every model of the bundle contains a moral error (the Germans'); the proof's witness model also contains evil, which the type does not require. The first precept's self-evidence (a.2, per se nota) is the candidate AQUINAS-FIRST-PRECEPT-SELF-EVIDENT, which connects the moral nodes to the premise program.
